Subject: Carver Capital — model residency & activation SLA exception request

Team — looping you in on an urgent ask from Carver (Emily copied). They are at the final stages of procurement and the contract asks for an activation SLA and a short residency guarantee for a small pool of models tied to their tenant. Specific asks from their side: 

- A 4-week warm residency window on a dedicated pool for their tenant for the first 90 days after go-live.
- A 99th percentile tail latency SLA of 250ms for their primary inference path (text-generation short prompts).
- A rollback/fallback policy to a quantized variant if full-precision capacity is constrained.

They understand this is out-of-the-box for Dedicated customers but are requesting an exception/fast-track to Reserved-style guarantees for an initial period while they ramp. Attached: Carver_SOW_v3.pdf with the proposed commercial terms.

High-level ask from us to Product/Eng: can we commit to a temporary residency guard (4 weeks) and a latency target for this deal? If not full SLA, what are the minimum gating controls we can offer (affinity pinning, prioritized scheduling, telemetry hooks)? Also, we need a clear owner and timeline to include in the SOW.

Next step I propose: quick triage call today or tomorrow to agree feasibility and an owner — can Marissa/Karthik/Ben confirm availability? Emily — would a go-live window of Nov 9–16 be accurate for your expected schedule?

Thanks,
Lauren

Thanks Lauren — quick read-through notes from Product: 

- Residency: we can support a short-term affinity/residency shim (warm pool) but it will require a pinned allocation on Dedicated-like hosts to meet the latency ask. That has cost/booking implications — need Sales to confirm whether Carver will accept an uplift for the reservation.
- Latency SLA: 250ms p99 is tight depending on prompt length and model family (we need model name). For a 32-token median prompt on a smaller open model (e.g., mix of Llama2-13B variants) it might be achievable with careful pinning and KV cache pre-warm; for larger models it will be risky.
- Fallback: automated fallback to a quantized variant is feasible; we need a QA window to validate quality delta and an observable circuit-breaker.

Questions for Sales/Eng:
1) Which model(s) are they planning to use? (Emily)
2) Is Carver willing to accept a temporary price uplift for the warm-residency allocation?
3) How long do they expect peak QPS during initial ramp (Ben) — we need RPS profile to estimate pool size.

I can set up a brief engineering scoping session with Karthik if we get QPS + model family.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Product, Serving

Adding engineering perspective — quick engineering notes and constraints: 

- If they want a 4-week contiguous residency with p99=250ms, we need to provision a small Dedicated pool sized to their QPS and lock it to their tenant. That requires a capacity reservation ticket and confirmation of commit (billing uplift).
- We can implement an "affinity pin" that pins the tenant to specific worker instances and preloads KV cache, reducing cold starts. This is low dev effort (configuration + scheduling rule).
- Autoscaling during the 4-week window will need to be constrained; we'll need an explicit override to avoid eviction. That is operationally doable but we must document rollback triggers.

Ben — can you share the expected peak RPS and token-per-request distribution? I opened a stub ticket: https://redwoodhq.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-9876 to track eng work and QA.

Attachment: residency-capacity-plan.csv (csv)

Thanks, all — apologies for the slight delay. Answers below: 

1) Model family: We will start with an open 13B family (custom small ensemble of Llama2-13B variants) and may evaluate a larger model after month 2.
2) Uplift: Carver is open to a one-time reservation uplift for a warm-residency if it buys us predictable performance during our first 90-day ramp. Please give us a ballpark uplift estimate.
3) Traffic profile: expected peak ~18 RPS during business hours in week 1, tapering to 6–8 RPS steady-state. Median prompt length ~28 tokens; 95th percentile ~120 tokens.

Go-live target: Nov 12 (week of Nov 9–16) — yes, that timing works for our procurement timeline.

We are comfortable with a fallback to a quantized variant provided we have an automated A/B quality check and a rollback window if quality drops more than X% (we can define X in the SOW).

Thanks — Emily
